label: TERRAIN CONTEXT · VISUAL
frame: bundle grid axes (x toward 90 E, y toward 0 E), metres, relative to the dataset site point; rows south-to-north

local.note: matches dataset.dem of the bundle; values are NOT copied here

regional.cropHashCheck: not reproducible from the bundle: values are stored rounded to 1e-4 m, the hash is of the unrounded crop
regional.role: display context around the 5 m crop; the solver reads its own copy, never this file

mid.product: NASA PGDA 78 5 m tile blended with the NASA GSFC SfS surface where it exists, 4 x 4 block means (20 m)
mid.rule: 5 m display height = (1 - w) LOLA + w SfS (w feathered over 200 m at the SfS edge); node = mean of the 4 x 4 pixels of its block; any non-finite pixel -> NaN (no fill); blocks on the tile pixel lattice
mid.role: L1 display terrain between the 5 m crop and the 80 m crop; the solver never reads it

localDisplay.product: NASA GSFC SfS elevation A306_GLDELEV_005 (Artemis III candidate region 6, Connecting Ridge), 5 m
localDisplay.citation: Bertone, S., McKenna, T. E., Barker, M. K., Mazarico, E., Beyer, R. A., Petro, N. (2025), Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.17954508
localDisplay.rule: display height = (1 - w) LOLA crop + w SfS, w = clip(distance inside the SfS footprint / 200 m, 0, 1); nodes are the bundle crop nodes
localDisplay.role: DISPLAY surface only. The solver, margins, ray hits and every number use the LOLA crop in the bundle, not this.

horizon.azimuthRule: index k -> grid angle 360*k/K degrees from +y toward +x; direction (sin, cos)
horizon.layout: (K, m, m): index = (k*m + j)*m + i, j south-to-north

local.march: 5 m steps to 1200 m on the 5 m crop (80 m regional where the crop ends), then 80 m steps to 20 km on the regional crop

mid.march: 20 m steps to 4 km on L1, max with 80 m steps to 20 km on the regional crop

regional.march: 80 m steps to 20 km on the regional crop

horizon.model: surface points lifted by a display shadow bias, nearest-cell sampling, curvature d^2/2R with R = 1737400 m, finite crops

skylineCrossCheck.note: display march = nearest-cell, 5 m crop to 1.2 km then 80 m crop to 20 km; solver = full 5 m tile + 80 m to 280 km. Where the display is lower, the controlling terrain is outside the displayed crops. Display-consistency evidence only.

limitations: Display shading only: shadows come from the displayed crops (about 16 km), not from the solver's 280 km horizon.
Terrain beyond the regional crop casts nothing, so points near its edge are under-shadowed.
Never an input to visible/blocked states, margins or metrics; those come from the bundle.
8-bit angles (0.05 deg), K azimuths with linear interpolation, 10 m / 160 m node spacing.
